Updates

Short notes on what shipped for Amazon EVS, VMware Cloud on AWS and VCF, with a link to the source for each.

November 2026

Nov 24, 2026VCFVMwareAI

VCF 9.1.2 is out#

What

Broadcom shipped VCF 9.1.2 today. Most of it is aimed at getting AI and Kubernetes platforms up faster:

  • An AI infrastructure quickstart: one vCenter plugin configures the cluster, turns on Supervisor and builds a VKS cluster.
  • A VKS quickstart that gives you a working Supervisor and VKS cluster, plus a test environment with add-ons.
  • Chained VKr upgrades. Pick the version you want and VCF works out the steps to get there.
  • The GitOps service (Argo CD inside VCF) and vSAN's S3-compatible object storage are now GA. Both were tech previews in 9.1.1.

Why it matters

The object storage piece is the one I'd pay attention to even if AI isn't on your roadmap. Backups, logs and cloud-native apps can use S3 buckets on vSAN, so you don't need a separate object store for them.

Who it's for

Teams building private AI or Kubernetes platforms on VCF, and anyone who needs S3 storage on-prem.

Source
  • Broadcom blog: Announcing General Availability of VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.2
Nov 24, 2026vCloudOneVMwareCloud

New on vCloudOne: sizing calculators#

What

I've added three sizers to the site, one each for Amazon EVS, VMware Cloud on AWS and on-prem VCF. Drop in RVTools exports or type in workload totals and you get hosts, clusters and management overhead, with checks and an Excel export.

  • EVS Sizing: hosts and clusters for Amazon EVS.
  • VMC Sizing: SDDCs, clusters and hosts, with placement and DR per workload group, a topology diagram and a memory tiering estimate per cluster.
  • VCF Sizing: fleets, instances, domains and clusters on your own hardware, plus licensing and add-on overhead.

Why it matters

Everything runs in your browser, so customer data stays on your machine. The VMC and VCF sizers explain each default when you hover over it, and the Excel export keeps your settings so you can load the sizing again later. Use them for early numbers and to compare options, then confirm with the official tools.

Who it's for

Architects and partners who need a quick, defensible first sizing.

Nov 20, 2026VMware Cloud on AWSHyperscalersVMware

You can now raise the Elastic DRS storage warning#

What

The Elastic DRS storage warning used to be fixed at 65%. You can now move it up to 75% through the Autoscaler API.

Why it matters

If your SDDCs run storage-heavy, that 65% warning can go off during normal operation. Now you can set it closer to the point where you'd actually act. Because it's an API setting, it's easy to apply across several SDDCs.

Who it's for

Customers with storage-heavy SDDCs, and whoever automates their Elastic DRS policies.

Source
  • VMware Cloud on AWS release notes: November 20, 2026
Nov 17, 2026Amazon EVSHyperscalersVMware

Amazon EVS gets r7i hosts, external principal storage and an Agent Skill#

What

Amazon EVS now supports r7i.metal-24xl and r7i.metal-48xl for VCF 9.x. These are memory-optimized hosts with no local NVMe, so AWS also added support for external principal storage. In practice that means Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP instead of vSAN.

The EVS Deployment Orchestrator can create the FSx file system for you, and with FSx a simple deployment needs only 2 hosts. AWS also released an Agent Skill that gives AI assistants enough EVS knowledge to answer questions, suggest designs, write blueprints and run deployments through the orchestrator.

Why it matters

Until now you bought compute and vSAN storage together. With r7i and FSx you can size them separately: memory-heavy workloads don't pay for NVMe they won't use, and storage grows without adding hosts.

Who it's for

Customers with memory-heavy workloads, teams already on FSx for ONTAP, and anyone automating EVS builds.

Sources
  • AWS What's New: Amazon EVS launches support for r7i.metal instances, external principal storage, and an Agent Skill
  • GitHub: Solutions for Amazon EVS release v1.1.0
Nov 4, 2026VCFVMware

vSphere Express, Live Recovery and DR built into VCF#

What

Broadcom announced a few changes to the VCF portfolio:

  • vSphere Express, a new entry edition on vSphere 9 for up to 128 cores. It includes vMotion, HA, distributed switching and TPM security.
  • Two new Advanced Services: VMware Live Recovery for disaster and cyber recovery, and VMware Compliance and Configuration Management.
  • Disaster recovery built into VCF and VVF themselves, planned for the next release.

Why it matters

Express gives smaller sites a supported starting point that can move up to VVF or VCF later. Native DR could change how people design and license recovery, so I'll be watching for the next release.

Who it's for

Small sites and branch offices, and VCF customers working on DR, cyber recovery or compliance.

Sources
  • Broadcom blog: VCF portfolio update
  • Network World: Broadcom expands VMware Cloud Foundation with AI, security, and recovery capabilities

Sep 3, 2026VCFVMwareAI

VCF 9.1.1 lands the week of VMware Explore#

What

VCF 9.1.1 came out the same week as VMware Explore in Las Vegas. The new features are mostly AI:

  • Multi-Tenant Model Sharing lets several business units use one model deployment while keeping their data separate.
  • AI Assistant for VCF is a chat assistant inside VCF Operations, and you choose the model provider.
  • GitOps and native object storage showed up as tech previews. Both went GA in 9.1.2.

Why it matters

For most infrastructure teams, 9.1.1 is simply the maintenance build to land on after 9.1. The AI features need VCF Private AI Services, so they matter most if private AI is already on your plan.

Who it's for

VCF customers planning their 9.1 upgrade, and teams running private AI on VCF.

Source

August 2026

Aug 27, 2026Amazon EVSHyperscalersVMware

i7i.metal-48xl and the EVS Deployment Orchestrator#

What

Two things landed around EVS's first birthday. The i7i.metal-48xl is a bigger host on 5th Gen Intel Xeon, so you can run more VMs on fewer hosts. AWS says i7i gives up to 23% better compute and more than 10% better price performance than i4i.

AWS also released the EVS Deployment Orchestrator (EDO) in the Solutions for Amazon EVS repo. You launch one CloudFormation stack and it builds the AWS networking, the hosts and VCF 9.0 or 9.1. A full build takes about 4 to 7 hours and runs unattended.

Why it matters

The 48xl is double the 24xl, which helps big clusters and memory tiering designs fit inside the 32-host limit. For VCF 9 you install VCF yourself with the VCF Installer, so EDO is the easy way to get a repeatable, hands-off build.

Who it's for

Larger EVS deployments, VCF 9 adopters, and teams that want builds they can repeat.

Sources
  • AWS What's New: Amazon EVS now supports i7i.metal-48xl
  • AWS blog: A year of expanding choice for VMware customers on AWS
  • AWS blog: One Stack, Full VCF: Deploying VCF 9 on Amazon EVS with the EVS Deployment Orchestrator
Aug 21, 2026Amazon EVSHyperscalersVMware

Three good reads: NSX Federation, DR and memory tiering on EVS#

What

AWS put out three design posts in one week:

  • Aug 18: NSX Federation on EVS. One Global Manager spans on-prem and EVS sites, with shared segments and firewall policy.
  • Aug 19: A walk-through of DR options for VMware workloads on EVS, from nothing pre-deployed to a full standby cluster.
  • Aug 21: Using VCF 9 memory tiering to fit more VMs on each host.

Why it matters

These cover the questions that usually come up after the migration is done: stretching networks and security across sites, how much standby capacity DR really needs, and how far tiering can push density. One thing to remember on EVS is that NVMe you give to memory tiering comes out of vSAN, so size tiering and storage together.

Who it's for

Anyone designing multi-site, DR or high-density EVS environments.

Sources
  • AWS blog: Amazon EVS with NSX Federation for Disaster Recovery and Multi-site Networking
  • AWS blog: Disaster Recovery for VMware Workloads on Amazon EVS
  • AWS blog: Increase your cluster density with Memory Tiering in Amazon EVS

Jul 6, 2026Amazon EVSHyperscalersVMware

Amazon EVS now runs VCF 9.0 and 9.1#

What

This is the big one for EVS this year. You can now run VCF 9.0 and 9.1 in every Region where EVS is available. EVS sets up the hosts and VPC networking, and you install VCF with Broadcom's VCF Installer. VCF evaluation mode is supported too, which is handy for proofs of concept.

Why it matters

VCF 9 brings memory tiering and the rest of the 9.x platform to AWS. Since the VCF install is now your job, have the installer steps and your VCF subscription sorted before the hosts are ready.

Who it's for

Customers moving to VCF 9 who want to run it on AWS, and anyone who wants memory tiering on EVS.

Sources
  • AWS What's New: Amazon EVS VCF 9.0 and 9.1 support
  • AWS blog: Announcing support for VCF 9.0 and 9.1 on Amazon EVS

May 5, 2026VCFVMwareAI

VCF 9.1 is here#

What

Broadcom announced VCF 9.1, the first feature release since 9.0, and it went GA later in May with an in-place upgrade from 9.0. The parts I'd look at first:

  • Better memory tiering. You can turn it on without a reboot, and you can mirror the tier device in software.
  • vSAN deduplication and compression on more cluster types.
  • Live patching for ESX on TPM-enabled hosts, continuous compliance, and ransomware recovery on-prem.
  • Bigger fleet and upgrade limits per VCF instance, faster VM and Kubernetes deployment, and S3 object storage as a tech preview.

Why it matters

9.1 is where memory tiering becomes practical for production. No reboot to enable it, and mirroring protects you if a tier drive fails, without needing a RAID controller. It's also one of the versions Amazon EVS added in July.

Who it's for

Every VCF customer. 9.1 is the current release and the upgrade target from 9.0.

Sources
  • Broadcom blog: VCF 9.1: The Secure, Cost-Effective Private Cloud Platform for Production AI
  • VCF 9.1 release notes: What's New

Apr 20, 2026Amazon EVSHyperscalersVMware

Windows Server licenses on Amazon EVS#

What

You can now get Windows Server licenses from AWS for VMs on EVS, whether you migrate them or build them new. You add an entitlement per VM through an EVS vCenter connector, and billing is per vCPU-hour while the VM runs.

Why it matters

VMs without license portability rights used to need a separate licensing plan. Now you can cover them in EVS and remove the entitlement when you no longer need it. VMs where you bring your own license don't cost anything extra from AWS.

Who it's for

EVS customers with Windows Server VMs that lack portability rights.

Sources
  • AWS What's New: Amazon EVS now offers Microsoft Windows Server Licensing
  • AWS blog: Windows Server licensing step-by-step guide

Apr 1, 2026VMware Cloud on AWSHyperscalersVMware

i7i.metal-24xl comes to VMware Cloud on AWS#

What

With SDDC 1.26v2, VMC supports i7i.metal-24xl for new and existing SDDCs in select Regions. It comes with host-to-host encryption, vSAN data-at-rest encryption and Intel TME memory encryption.

A few things to know: existing SDDCs need to be on 1.26v2 first, vSAN ESA is only for new SDDCs or new secondary clusters, hyper-threading is on by default (96 logical cores per host), and stretched clusters on i7i use vSAN OSA.

Why it matters

It gives i3, i3en and i4i customers a newer host to move to, as well as an option for new SDDCs.

Who it's for

VMC customers planning a host refresh, and new SDDC deployments.

Sources
  • Broadcom blog: Announcing the i7i.metal-24xl Instance for VMware Cloud on AWS
  • VMware Cloud on AWS release notes: April 1, 2026

March 2026

Mar 25, 2026vCloudOneHyperscalersVMware

Amazon EVS deployment prerequisites guide#

What

I wrote up everything EVS checks before it deploys VCF 5.x, in the order you'll need it: account and support plan, IAM, IP planning, VPC and subnets, Route 53, DHCP, VPC Route Server and BGP, capacity reservations, licensing and key pairs. It comes with a Terraform kit and a prerequisite validator.

Why it matters

EVS validates everything up front and fails fast if something is missing, so getting the prep right the first time saves a lot of back and forth. For VCF 9, use the VCF Installer or the EVS Deployment Orchestrator instead.

Who it's for

Anyone preparing a first EVS deployment on VCF 5.x.

VCF 9.0.2 maintenance release#

What

A fix release for VCF 9.0. Two changes in vCenter 9.0.2 stood out to me: certificates issued by the VMware Certificate Authority for vCenter and ESX now renew automatically before they expire, and Supervisor control plane backup is on by default.

Jan 16, 2026VMware Cloud on AWSHyperscalersVMware

SDDC 1.26: vSAN ESA, bring your own key and VM hardware 21#

What

SDDC 1.26 moves VMC to vSphere 8.0 Update 3 and brings a lot with it:

  • vSAN ESA is GA, with RAID-5 from 3 hosts. It's the default for new i4i deployments, for non-stretched SDDCs only.
  • Bring your own key: VM encryption with an external KMIP key management system.
  • VM hardware version 21, with up to 256 disks per VM and NVMe for Windows Server Failover Clustering.
  • VMware Tools 12.5.4.

Why it matters

ESA changes how you size VMC. Every drive is capacity and RAID-5 starts at three hosts, so small clusters get more usable storage than they did on OSA. Stretched SDDCs stay on OSA.

Who it's for

Every VMC customer, especially new i4i SDDCs and anyone who needs to manage their own encryption keys.

Sources
  • Broadcom blog: VMware Cloud on AWS: SDDC Version 1.26 Release
  • VMware Cloud on AWS release notes: January 16, 2026

Dec 2, 2025VMware Cloud on AWSHyperscalersVMware

VMware Cloud on AWS: December 2025 roundup#

What

Broadcom's December roundup covered a few changes:

  • A redesigned console at vmc.broadcom.com.
  • Stretched clusters can now scale down to 4 hosts (2 per AZ) or 2 hosts (1 per AZ), with some limits.
  • HCX 4.11.3 drops WAN optimization and is supported until October 11, 2027.
  • Better estimates for moving from i3.metal to i3en.metal or i4i.metal.

Why it matters

Smaller stretched clusters make a multi-AZ SDDC cheaper to start with. And if you use HCX WAN-OPT, plan to remove it before upgrading.

Who it's for

Customers on stretched clusters or HCX, and anyone still on i3.metal.

Source
  • Broadcom blog: VMware Cloud on AWS: What's New (December 2025)
